title: First Light SDK Playground — heuristics and ops sketch
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, operationally-focused sketch for the 'First Light' SDK playground we want to ship into the developer console and docs in Q1. Target audience: engineers trying Redwood API for the first time (trial users, PoCs, internal demos). Goal is low cognitive load + obvious safety nets for common failure modes (auth, rate limits, streaming disconnects).

High-level constraints (decision drivers):
- 5 minute happy path to see a generated response in a minimal app (CLI + tiny React sandbox).
- Local reproducibility: dev can run a tiny mock server with same SDK call surface (no GPU required).
- Observability hooks surfaced in the quickstart: how to see latency, cost, and tokens.
- Ops playbook attached for the top 4 incidents we see during onboarding flows.

Core deliverables (MVP):
- CLI quickstart: single-file example (node/python) that demonstrates auth, one-shot prompt, and token breakdown.
- Mini-react playground: embedded component with a streaming experience and retry button.
- Trouble-shooting checklist: quick fixes for 401/429/timeout/long-tail tokens.
- Incident runbook (short): triage guide when users are stuck on 'no response' or 'very slow tokens'.
- Evaluation harness: 10 prompts and expected shapes for regression checks.

Quickstart lab templates (three small labs):
1) Hello-LLM CLI (3 steps)
  - Step 0: setup env var (REDWOOD_API_KEY) + pip/npm install redwood-sdk-preview
  - Step 1: paste sample code: simple call -> print text -> include token usage printout
  - Step 2: intentionally trigger a 401 by unsetting key and show error output and guidance
  - Learning outcome: see request lifecycle, learn where to check key and quotas
  - Ops note: add a debug flag to the CLI that prints request-id header for support

2) Streaming micro-playground (browser sandbox)
  - Minimal UI: input, send button, streaming result area, retry + cancel
  - Feature: incremental token counter displayed, with TTL cache hint when prefix cached
  - Failure modes to demo: network interruption, model fallback to cheaper variant (config toggle)
  - Observability: console shows tracing id + latency; link to Console route for this model

3) Embeddings quick-check (sheet integration)
  - Short lab that shows calling embedding endpoint, inserting vectors into a JS array and doing naive cosine search in the client (for demo only)
  - Safety note: push to server for production; explain vector dimensionality and cost units

Heuristics & UX guardrails (notes-to-self):
- Always surface request-id and model-version in the quickstart UI. Customers call support, we must have those to tie logs.
- Default to a cheap-but-compatible model for 1st run (reduces cost shock). Clear CTA to upgrade model.
- Show token counts pre/post request in the UI so users understand per-token billing.
- Make the default timeout conservative (6s) but explain how to tune for long completions.
- Streaming: show partial results immediately, but keep a visual indicator if the model is still computing (spinner + token rate).

Observability checklist to include in docs:
- Enable DEBUG env for SDK to print request-id and timings.
- Where to find the request in Redwood Console: Model route -> Requests -> filter by request-id.
- Token/cost telemetry: link short explainer and an example snapshot.
- How to capture a full reproducible report when filing a bug (code snippet, request-id, model name, sequence length, prompt).

Incident playbook (top onboarding incidents)
1) 401 invalid key
  - Symptoms: immediate 401 from first call
  - Quick triage: check REDWOOD_API_KEY env, look for revoked key events in console -> API keys page
  - Escalation: if key present but 401 persists, ask for request-id and timestamp, open ENG-SEC ticket if suspected compromise

2) 429 quota or rate limit
  - Symptoms: 429s once usage ramps in quickstart labs
  - Quick triage: check user's plan in account -> show they hit free credits or per-minute rate cap
  - Mitigation: suggest temporarily lowering concurrency / adding exponential backoff in sample SDK wrapper

3) Streaming disconnects / partial responses
  - Symptoms: partial text then stream drops or client shows socket error
  - Quick triage: reproduce locally with curl to check network vs SDK behavior; capture request-id header
  - Mitigation: add retry button, and for automatic retries, prefer idempotent wrapper flows or resume via KV cache when supported

4) Very slow token generation (tail latency)
  - Symptoms: tokens streaming slowly; total time > expected SLO
  - Quick triage: check model variant, sequence length, and platform region; look for cold-start logs on dedicted nodes
  - Mitigation: recommend switching to a lower-latency variant in the playground (UI toggle), show batching and caching tips in Optimize guide link

Gating checklist before marking 'First Light' as ready for public docs: (short)
- [ ] Lab code is < 120 LOC each, linted, with CI smoke tests (node + python).
- [ ] Embedded sandbox isolated by iframe + CORS + limited rate in Console sandbox account.
- [ ] Clear guidance for PIIs and sample prompts that avoid sensitive data.
- [ ] Support playbook + triage form ready and linked from quickstart.
- [ ] Mini-eval: run 10 prompts through hosted/cheap model and record latency/cost numbers in the doc.

Samples and snippets (to paste into the quickstart)
- Minimal Node snippet (pseudocode):
  const r = await redwood.generate({model: 'redwood-fast-1', prompt: 'Write a two-line haiku about debugging'});
  console.log(r.text);
  console.log('tokens', r.tokens, 'request-id', r.request_id);

- Retry wrapper pattern (psuedocode):
  async function resilientGenerate(prompt) {
    for (let i=0;i<3;i++) {
      try { return await r.generate(prompt); } catch (e) { if (e.code === '429') await sleep(2**i * 100); else throw e }
    }
  }

Open questions / followups (internal):
- Do we want the CLI to be part of the main SDK repo or a separate examples repo? pros/cons noted in ENG-3245.
- Does the Console sandbox get its own rate limits, or share tenant defaults? Need infra decision from SRE.
- Should the playground show cost estimates in USD per request or only token counts? Ops leaning: show tokens + explain cost calculator link.
- UX: ephemeral keys vs instructing users to create their own API key in the onboarding flow. Tradeoffs: friction vs security.

Action items (next steps):
- Priya: draft the CLI example and open PR to examples repo (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Evan: prototype the streaming component and wire request-id into UI (ETA: 1 week).
- María: write the incident triage template and add to support playbook (ETA: 1 week).
- Samir: add CI smoke test matrix and small latency benchmark jobs (ETA: 2 weeks).

Notes-to-self / rough editing marks:
- Keep language informal in the playground; add an "if you break things, here's how to recover" short card.
- Avoid heavy product claims in the first-run docs; focus on reproducibility and how to graduate to production flows.
- Circle back with SRE on sandbox rate-limits before public rollout.

References and related:
- onboarding metrics doc (todo link)
- ENG-3245 (discussion thread about example repo layout)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/87 (streaming component prototype)

End of sketch.
_notes: informal doc: working sketch to be converted to a polished quickstart and embedded playground module. Keep iterations in this doc until final PR is merged.
